query: Add a docstring to: def fetch_rows(table: str, limit: int = 100) -> list[dict]: which raises ConnectionError if the DB is unreachable and returns the rows.
expected_behavior: Uses triple double quotes with a one-line summary ending in a period
Uses Google-style Args:, Returns: and Raises: sections
Does not repeat types in Args because the signature is annotated
Uses descriptive voice ('Fetches rows...') unless the file already uses imperative

query: Document def restock(items, name, quantity): which raises ValueError if quantity <= 0 and returns the new count. No annotations exist.
expected_behavior: Puts types in parentheses in Args and Returns because the signature has none
Includes a Raises: ValueError entry
Does not modify the function body or signature

query: Document this generator function and the class it lives in: class Reader with attributes path and encoding; def lines(self): yields each stripped line.
expected_behavior: Uses Yields: instead of Returns: for the generator
Class docstring has an Attributes: section for public attributes
Does not document __init__ separately when the class docstring covers its arguments

query: Should I write docstrings for a @override method that does the same as its parent, and for a private two-line helper _norm(x)?
expected_behavior: Says an @override method needs no docstring unless its behavior differs materially
Says a short obviously-named private helper may use a one-line docstring or none
Does not demand full Args/Returns sections for trivial code

query: Write a NumPy-style docstring for def area(w: float, h: float) -> float.
expected_behavior: Reads and follows the NumPy reference: Parameters and Returns headings underlined with hyphens
Uses 'name : type' form for parameters
Does not mix in Google-style Args: sections

query: This file's docstrings all use :param x: and :returns: fields. Add one for def scale(v, k).
expected_behavior: Detects the existing Sphinx style and uses it instead of defaulting to Google
Uses :param:, :type:, :returns: and :rtype: fields without blank lines between them
